title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Converting an Account to Another Tier
content:
An existing Savings & Money Market Accounts product can be moved to a different tier without opening a new account. This page states what a conversion changes, what the account and the customer must satisfy, and what it does to fees, promotions and the early closure window.

## Rule

**What changes.** A conversion alters the tier only. The account number, the balance and the account's history all carry over unchanged.

**Status.** The account has to be in active status at the moment the conversion is recorded, as the bank's account record shows.

**Entry tests of the target tier.** On the conversion date the customer has to meet the target tier's own entry requirements, including any Personal Checking tier it demands and the limits on how many accounts a customer may hold, with one substitution: in place of the opening-deposit test, the money already in the account has to reach the target tier's smallest first deposit.

**Charges.** No fee is charged for a conversion.

**Promotions and early closure.** Any promotional period on the account ends on the conversion date. The early closure window is not started afresh; it keeps running from the original opening date.

**Frequency.** An account can be converted at most once in a statement cycle.

## Eligibility checklist on the conversion date

| Item | Must hold |
|---|---|
| Account status | active |
| Customer's age | reaches the target tier's minimum opening age |
| Required checking tier, if the target names one | the customer has an active checking account of a named tier |
| Account-count limits | the customer is within the family limit and the target tier's per-customer limit |
| Balance | the current balance is at least the target tier's smallest first deposit |
| Conversions this cycle | none recorded yet for the account |

## Points of judgement

**Does converting restart the early closure window?** No. The window is always measured from the day the account was first opened.

**The account earned a promotional rate. Does the rate follow it into the new tier?** No; a conversion brings the promotional period to an end on the day it is recorded.

**Is the balance test the same as a first deposit?** It stands in for it: the balance already in the account is compared with the target tier's smallest first deposit, and no new deposit is needed.
